activity.scenario: Original hypothetical: one neighbor enjoys music while working; another needs quiet to concentrate. They share a wall. For this exercise these preferences are stipulated facts, not measured evidence. The available arrangements and their effects remain assumptions.
activity.definitions: Interpretation: a reading of the source. Empirical assumption: a testable claim about the situation. Normative addition: a claim about what people ought to do. Proposed conclusion: an action supported by the selected reasons; no automatic moral score is assigned.

premises.text: Ask whether imposing an unwanted interruption would be acceptable in the relevant reversed position.
Give the affected person’s actual need for concentration weight, rather than projecting the actor’s musical taste.
Headphones or another room are available and would reduce the disturbance without creating a comparable burden.
Read the directive as a reason to attend to how the other person would want to be treated in this setting.
Ask about the other person’s needs and seek terms both can reasonably accept.
A conversation and a workable quiet/music schedule are feasible here.

actions.label: Use headphones or move the music
actions.objection: This depends on a feasible alternative and a judgment about competing needs. The quoted words alone do not establish either.

actions.label: Ask and negotiate quiet/music times
actions.objection: Asking alone does not guarantee a fair agreement; a power imbalance or an essential need could remain.

actions.label: Continue playing music unchanged
actions.objection: Enjoying music yourself does not establish that the other person welcomes it. Explain why the affected person’s different preference can be set aside.

guides.title: An editorial reconstruction of restraint
guides.conclusion: On these added premises, choose a feasible arrangement that avoids imposing the unwanted interruption.
guides.objection: What counts as the relevant reversed position, and how competing needs should be weighed, remains contestable.

guides.title: An editorial reconstruction of responsive attention
guides.conclusion: On these added premises, ask about needs and negotiate an acceptable arrangement.
guides.objection: The actor can still project personal preferences, and consultation alone may leave unfair terms.

activity.transfer: Apply one reconstruction to a shared office where one person prefers a bright light and another is sensitive to glare. Identify what you would need to learn before recommending an action.

Does reciprocity settle a disagreement?

Two passages, different preferences, and the premises between them.

Build a reasoned response to a disagreement over music and quiet. Separate the source words from assumptions you add, then test what changes when the roles reverse.

Local review covers source fidelity, evidence labeling and bounded prototype reuse. No professional specialist, screen-reader or learner session has been performed.

Two English textual witnesses and an original hypothetical. This does not survey either tradition or establish historical influence.

  1. Read the sources
  2. Explore the evidence
  3. Explain a limitation
01

Read closely

Confucius as represented in the Analects; James Legge, translator

Reciprocity in an exchange

Quotation

What you do not want done to yourself, do not do to others.

Editorial context: Tsze-kung asks for a rule to practise throughout life; the Master names reciprocity. These are Legge’s translated words in a transmitted dialogue, not an independently authenticated recording of a historical utterance.

Source and reuse details

Confucian Analects, translated by James Legge

Book XV, CHAP. XXIII; ebook 3330 · Digital release 2002-07-01; updated 2021-01-08; print witness not verified

Gutenberg catalog identifies public domain in the USA. Translator died in 1897. Short unchanged attributed text selected for this local critical exercise.

USA text-reuse evidence; worldwide full-text distribution is not established. No Gutenberg package, branding or images imported.

Jesus’s teaching as presented in Matthew; World English Bible translators

A directive in a teaching sequence

Quotation

Therefore, whatever you desire for men to do to you, you shall also do to them; for this is the law and the prophets.

Editorial context: Verses 7–11 concern asking, seeking and knocking, parental bread/fish comparisons and the Father in heaven giving good things. Verse 12 follows with “Therefore”; the chapter closes by presenting Jesus as teacher. The exercise does not require religious assent.

Source and reuse details

World English Bible Classic: Matthew 7

7:12, read with 7:7–12 and 7:28–29 · 2020 stable text edition; HTML inspected 2026-10-22

Publisher public-domain dedication in its official rights statement; unchanged verse, attributed to the Classic edition.

Only unchanged English text. Editorial premises are separate; no logo, audio or endorsement.

What this exploration can establish

  • The selected Legge ebook labels the exchange XV.XXIII. The corresponding exchange is 15.24 in Eno’s 2015 English teaching translation, p.85. This resolves this pair of locators only; no reason for the discrepancy or universal modern numbering is asserted.
  • No Chinese or Greek original has been verified. Translation choices can affect this comparison.
  • The SEP discussion cautions that removing dialogue context can distort comparison. Neither short passage exhausts Confucian or Christian ethics.
  • A premise is a reason offered for a conclusion. An objection identifies a disputed premise or inference; it need not reject the whole source.
Supplemental research and rights references

Robert Eno, The Analects of Confucius: An Online Teaching Translation — Printed p.85, passage 15.24 (PDF page index 99). Supplemental numbering reference; not a Chinese critical-edition check.

Confucius — Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Section 4. Supplemental context; no endorsement or exhaustive account.

World English Bible Classic: rights and edition statement — Public-domain declaration and 2020 stable text edition. The edition name must not label altered text as verbatim WEB.

02

Explore the evidence

Original hypothetical: one neighbor enjoys music while working; another needs quiet to concentrate. They share a wall. For this exercise these preferences are stipulated facts, not measured evidence. The available arrangements and their effects remain assumptions.

Interpretation: a reading of the source. Empirical assumption: a testable claim about the situation. Normative addition: a claim about what people ought to do. Proposed conclusion: an action supported by the selected reasons; no automatic moral score is assigned.

Build your ordered premise list

Add a premise, then use Move up, Move down or Remove. Every premise below is editorial, separate from the quotation and stipulated facts.

    Read both complete editorial reconstructions

    An editorial reconstruction of restraint

    Source: Reciprocity in an exchange. The scenario facts above are stipulated.

    1. Interpretation: Ask whether imposing an unwanted interruption would be acceptable in the relevant reversed position.
    2. Normative addition: Give the affected person’s actual need for concentration weight, rather than projecting the actor’s musical taste.
    3. Empirical assumption: Headphones or another room are available and would reduce the disturbance without creating a comparable burden.

    Proposed conclusion: On these added premises, choose a feasible arrangement that avoids imposing the unwanted interruption.

    Objection: What counts as the relevant reversed position, and how competing needs should be weighed, remains contestable.

    An editorial reconstruction of responsive attention

    Source: A directive in a teaching sequence. The scenario facts above are stipulated.

    1. Interpretation: Read the directive as a reason to attend to how the other person would want to be treated in this setting.
    2. Normative addition: Ask about the other person’s needs and seek terms both can reasonably accept.
    3. Empirical assumption: A conversation and a workable quiet/music schedule are feasible here.

    Proposed conclusion: On these added premises, ask about needs and negotiate an acceptable arrangement.

    Objection: The actor can still project personal preferences, and consultation alone may leave unfair terms.

    These examples are not exclusive to either tradition. A source quotation does not automatically validate the added premises or proposed conclusion.

    One notebook for this exploration revision, up to 1,500 characters. Notes stay in this browser. Shared links contain selections only. Nothing is sent to a server.

    03

    Try the idea elsewhere

    Apply one reconstruction to a shared office where one person prefers a bright light and another is sensitive to glare. Identify what you would need to learn before recommending an action.

    What a careful explanation includes
    • Identify the selected textual witness and its setting.
    • Label source wording, stipulated facts, interpretation, empirical assumptions and normative additions separately.
    • Explain a proposed action and an objection; swapping roles must not silently swap the other person’s preferences.
    • Allow another defensible reconstruction. Neither example belongs exclusively to one tradition.

    There is no automatic score for your written interpretation. Use the guide to inspect your reasoning.

    Connections into the atlas

    Optional collection routes; these are not prerequisites or independent evidence for this task.

## Dimension decisions

**content — passed, bounded AI English source/context review.** Both quoted passages match the verified selected English bodies. Legge wording is an unchanged sentence within the exchange; context preserves Tsze-kung’s lifelong-practice question and the Master’s reciprocity answer. Matthew retains the full verse including Therefore and law-and-prophets conclusion, plus an accurately bounded explanation of 7:7–11 and 7:28–29. Reader assent is not presumed. Interpretive reconstructions, empirical assumptions and normative additions are explicitly editorial. The scenario states differing preferences and shared wall as stipulated facts. No unsupported original-language, historical-influence, moral-ranking or tradition-equivalence assertion appears. Both complete reconstructions include objections and are expressly nonexclusive to their traditions. The source comparison stays within these English witnesses.

**provenance — passed, bounded AI edition/locator review.** Legge actual selected locator remains XV.XXIII. The 2002/2021 dates are clearly digital-file dates; print witness unverified. Eno supplemental locator is expressly that specific English translation’s 15.24/p.85, not an asserted universal numbering or Chinese critical-edition verification. WEB edition identifies Classic/2020 stable text; no 2026 translation date is fabricated. No Chinese or Greek original is claimed inspected. Stopped ctext is neither used nor recovered. Supplemental sources remain links and original observations, distinct from selected textual witnesses.

**rights — passed only for the declared local prototype’s unchanged short text and original editorial exercise.** WEB publisher’s official copr.htm explicitly dedicates text to public domain and distinguishes edition trademark from altered text. The selected text remains verbatim, with all editorial material outside quotation. Legge catalog establishes USA public-domain evidence, with limited selection and attributed critical exercise; visible scope expressly does not establish worldwide full-text distribution. No Gutenberg package, scans, logo or recording is imported. Eno’s limited permissions are not misrepresented as unrestricted: no Eno translated passage or illustration is reproduced. SEP content is original contextual paraphrase/reference, with no article text/assets imported. This pass is not worldwide republication clearance, legal advice, institutional endorsement, or approval of any later enlarged content/media selection.

**argument-learning design — scoped pass as AI desk review; no observed learning-effect claim.** Two defensible editorial reconstructions separate quoted source, stipulated facts, interpretation, empirical assumptions, normative addition and proposed conclusion. The objection panels identify disputed assumptions and unresolved conflicts rather than grading a source/tradition false. The bank supports ordering/removal; private notes and transfer prompt allow a reader to explain a different reconstruction. A changed actor perspective does not silently replace the other person’s taste. I directly exercised six pure-model combinations (two guides × three actions) and URL-state roundtrips: all retained state; all full-example feedback only reported inclusion of example premises and explicitly denied truth/moral necessity. The logic does not compute a validity or moral score and the UI explicitly says so. Missing-example-premise feedback allows omission with explanation, rather than declaring a competing interpretation wrong. This is adequate for the bounded formative activity; it is not a proof that the reconstruction is deductively valid or that learners understand it.
